items.title: Reliable attached-client baseline
acceptance: Run pinned tmux and freshly built zz with isolated homes/config roots and short sockets; record binary hashes, source revision and dirty state, OS, TERM, shell and dimensions.
Reproduce or explain the recorded macOS geometry-report timeout using retained attach, input, daemon and outer-screen diagnostics. A timeout or missing report fails the attempt.

Produce a repeatable baseline at 80x24, 100x24 and 120x24 with all measured differences and fixture limitations retained, including the waived wide-terminal columns. This package proves fixture reliability, not runtime parity.
items.evidence_note: Exploratory run on 2026-09-09 with existing target/debug/zz exited 2: zz geometry report did not happen within 10 seconds. The binary was not rebuilt or revision-attested. Earlier closed evidence records a Linux pass; neither result establishes a current portable baseline.
items.next_action: Read the geometry fixture, build and identify both binaries, then reproduce the timeout with retained diagnostics before changing runtime behavior.

items.title: Complete screen and interaction comparison
acceptance: Reuse existing attached-client drivers to compare all decoded cells, glyph widths, styles, cursor position/visibility/shape, geometry and resulting interaction state at named settled checkpoints.
Demonstrate that independent glyph, color/attribute, cursor and geometry changes fail with a useful location/state difference. Equivalent raw escape spellings must not fail.

Retain captures and environment at 80, 100, 109 and 120 columns, including small heights, split/zoom/resize and status off/on/multiple rows/top/bottom. Declare each controlled dynamic value and comparison rule.
items.evidence_note: Current fixtures compare selected status rows, dimensions, markers and daemon facts. Some attached assertions accept different zz and tmux indicators. A complete screen/cursor comparison has not been demonstrated.
items.next_action: Identify the smallest extension of the existing PTY driver that captures decoded cells and cursor state; freeze its comparison channels and failure examples.

items.title: Stock launcher, command and key behavior
acceptance: With clean config roots, compare bare packaged launch, attach and new-session on empty/live servers plus new-window and split-window. Assert stdout/stderr/exits, selected targets, pane kinds and the complete attached screen.
Drive unmodified stock split, chooser, rename, selection, zoom and detach bindings through actual stdin. Direct split-window creating a terminal does not substitute for testing its stock binding.

Test root bindings and application keys overlapping Ctrl-\ and Alt-s/Alt-S. Chrome cannot consume them outside its owning context. Exercise explicit config roots, -f and existing zz layering separately and record any policy conflict.
items.evidence_note: Source inspection found bare launcher new-session -A, stock bindings using native picker/sidebar commands, and chrome shortcuts before daemon routing. Explicit split-window already creates terminals. Accepted default-key decisions do not establish the new contract.
items.next_action: Capture unmodified tmux and zz launch/key behavior, then separate shared command/key policy from client presentation without adding a compatibility profile.

items.title: Default canvas, status and pane borders
acceptance: Ordinary tmux commands preserve the pinned canvas at narrow and wide dimensions; width never invokes the sidebar. Cover split, zoom, pane-border-status, small heights and resize restoration.
Compare full status/border presentation for default/custom formats, top/bottom/off/multiple rows, named/indexed/RGB colors, theme options and terminal light/dark reports.
Compare copy/view/prefix indicators and message/prompt restoration without waiving cells occupied by zz hints. Turn the three recorded theme differences into asserted comparisons.
items.evidence_note: On 2026-09-09 the existing debug binary passed all 11 status-row assertions; three theme cases differed and were record-only. Sidebar visibility still starts at 109 columns. This exploratory pass had no freshly built candidate and covers selected rows only.
items.next_action: Extend the measured default canvas through the sidebar threshold and carry the existing tui.status-row gap into full-screen acceptance.

items.title: Pane copy mode and search
acceptance: Compare stock emacs and vi pane copy tables, forward/backward search editing, repeat search, numeric counts, line/page movement, selection, rectangles, copy and cancel through actual input.
Assert cells, mode/search prompts, cursor, selection styles and resulting paste-buffer bytes, including live mode/binding changes and return to terminal input.
Keep ordinary pane search proof separate from command-output search. Inventory remaining copy actions against their existing authority before claiming complete table coverage.
items.evidence_note: Command-output search editing works, but ordinary pane TerminalUiCommand search reports terminal search is unsupported here. Existing copy closures cover narrower contracts.
items.next_action: Reproduce stock forward/backward search in an ordinary pane, then identify existing proof for each pane-copy acceptance clause.

items.title: Chooser and command-output presentation
acceptance: Compare choose-tree, choose-buffer, find-window and long command output with stock bindings: screen extent, status retention, titles, rows, shortcuts, previews, tagging, filtering, help and scrolling.
Compare output search and prompt lifecycle without replacement zz-only bindings, including selection/copy and return to the underlying pane.
Retain behavioral coverage while replacing alternate zz/tmux marker expectations with whole-screen evidence for the claimed surfaces.
items.evidence_note: The renderer has custom chooser title/footer and output header/geometry. Existing attached checks use separate indicator expectations and one native search binding, so their navigation pass is not full presentation proof.
items.next_action: Capture default choose-tree and long command output on both clients; classify differences in layout, content, style and input.

items.title: Prompts, menus, popups and pane labels
acceptance: Compare command-prompt, confirm-before, display-menu, display-popup and display-panes placement, clipping/wrapping, title/style, cursor, configured keys and size changes.
Exercise nested surfaces/messages, keyboard and mouse cancellation/selection, restoration and no input delivery to covered panes.
Reuse existing behavioral closures as regressions and independently measure complete output at the final candidate.
items.evidence_note: Existing attached fixtures cover several overlay behaviors but do not claim whole-screen equality. Prompt placement currently depends on sidebar visibility.
items.next_action: Inventory existing overlay cases and add whole-screen checkpoints to a small prompt and popup case before broadening.

items.title: Mouse, paste, focus and key ownership
acceptance: Compare stock/custom root and copy mouse bindings, drag selection, border resize, status clicks, wheel and double/triple clicks with mouse on/off and application tracking.
Assert target, action, screen and no unintended input leakage across copy mode, prompts, choosers and popups. Cover paste, focus and supported repeat/release paths.
Reassess the TUI portion of accepted native-mouse decisions while preserving explicit zz bindings and other clients.
items.evidence_note: The registry accepts client-owned gestures instead of several stock mouse entries. Current input gates mux/application tracking, but the full interaction matrix has not been run.
items.next_action: Select one stock root mouse binding and one copy gesture, record delivery and reference effects, then expand the table.

items.title: Outer-terminal capabilities and fidelity
acceptance: Declare a finite capability matrix covering legacy/extended keys, user keys, paste, focus/mouse, color/theme replies, Unicode widths and alternate-screen restoration.
Compare effects and client facts for cells/styles and global flags including -2, -u and -T. Ignored flags and waived capability cases remain visible obligations.
Preserve named/indexed/RGB color behavior under palette changes while accepting equivalent escape spelling. Expand coverage through explicit cases rather than claiming every terminal.
items.evidence_note: The TUI reconstructs cells/styles and uses terminal-name capability checks. The CLI consumes several terminal flags without applying them. Accepted negotiation/engine decisions require bounded remeasurement.
items.next_action: Write the capability matrix from the pin and tty setup, starting with one controlled legacy and one extended-key terminal.

items.title: Slow output, recovery and client lifecycle
acceptance: Measure prolonged terminal backpressure past the writer budget, deliver an observable bound key while undrained, and verify bounded memory and response within a declared reference-derived deadline.
Resume reading and compare the final screen. Detach under backlog and prove no queued paint appears after terminal restoration.
Exercise different-sized simultaneous terminal clients, read-only attach, detach/reattach and supported transport recovery. Compare selected targets, geometry, focus and final screen.
items.evidence_note: The short-backlog stdin fix is closed. The open queue-budget gap records 4 MiB saturation where zz input waits for drain after prolonged backlog; this campaign has not remeasured it.
items.next_action: Reuse the registered prolonged-backpressure reproduction and record current reference/zz behavior before choosing an output recovery change.

items.title: Remaining stock client command inventory
acceptance: Enumerate existing stock-client exceptions, including choose-client, clock-mode, customize-mode, suspend/lock, refresh and capture/output, into a finite command/flag roster.
For each entry compare exact stdout/stderr/exits and attached state/screen. Declare binary-output and unsupported-platform cases without counting them as parity.
Add stable child obligations for independent uncovered commands and retain this parent until the declared roster is proved.
items.evidence_note: The previous campaign accepts several native client-tool and transport choices. Everyday terminal and selected query tests cannot establish this remaining inventory.
items.next_action: Extract the command roster from the linked gaps and pin inventory; split independent command families before implementation.

items.title: Superset commands beside tmux behavior
acceptance: Invoke existing sidebar, picker, browser, Agent and editor commands directly and through user bindings. No compatibility profile or feature activation flag is required.
Exercise create/select/split/resize/detach/reattach around those commands. Standard commands retain their meaning and input ownership; withdrawing extra UI restores the expected terminal canvas.
Verify client-local sidebar state across clients and browser capability/provider fallback. Retain existing Agent/editor cards; new feature development is outside this obligation.
items.evidence_note: Sidebar and picker work today; browser frames require Kitty support and a provider. Agent/editor show cards. These surfaces have no tmux visual counterpart; proof concerns their declared commands and surrounding terminal behavior.
items.next_action: Freeze existing superset command behavior and add composition cases after ordinary terminal and input contracts have passing proof.
